description: Men's fashion colour matching rules for Urban Raja AI Stylist.

rules.description: Men's fashion colour matching rules for Urban Raja AI Stylist.

rules.reason: Black and beige create a balanced neutral contrast that looks clean and versatile.
Black and white create a classic high-contrast combination that is simple, versatile and easy to style.
White and blue create a clean and balanced combination. The contrast is noticeable without looking too loud.
Grey and black create a refined monochromatic combination with low visual noise. Different shades and textures can add depth to the outfit.
Olive and cream create a soft earthy combination. The muted contrast gives the outfit a relaxed and sophisticated appearance.
Blue and beige create a balanced combination between a cool colour and a warm neutral. It looks polished without being too formal.

rules.name: Light and dark balance
rules.guideline: Pairing a light colour with a dark colour usually creates clear visual contrast and makes an outfit easier to read.
rules.styling_tip: When using strong light-dark contrast, keep the remaining pieces relatively simple to avoid visual clutter.

rules.name: Monochromatic outfit
rules.guideline: A monochromatic outfit uses different shades, tones or tints from the same colour family.
rules.styling_tip: Use differences in shade, texture or fabric to prevent the outfit from looking flat.

rules.name: Neutral colour foundation
rules.guideline: Neutral colours are versatile and can usually be combined with other neutrals or stronger accent colours.
rules.styling_tip: Use neutral colours as the base of an outfit and add one stronger colour when you want more visual interest.

rules.name: Balance strong colours
rules.guideline: When an outfit contains a bright or highly saturated colour, balance it with neutral or muted colours.
rules.styling_tip: If one clothing piece is visually loud, keep the other major pieces relatively simple so the outfit does not become visually overwhelming.

rules.name: 60-30-10 colour balance
rules.guideline: A useful styling guideline is to use one dominant colour, one secondary colour and a smaller accent colour.
rules.styling_tip: The 60-30-10 approach is a guideline rather than a strict mathematical rule. Outfit proportions, patterns and textures can change the visual balance.

rules.name: Warm and cool colour balance
rules.guideline: Warm and cool colours can be combined successfully when their intensity and proportions are balanced. Neutral colours can help connect different colour temperatures.
rules.styling_tip: Use neutral colours when you want to make a warm-and-cool combination feel more cohesive.

rules.name: Limit multiple strong colours
rules.guideline: Using several highly saturated or visually dominant colours in one outfit can make the outfit look visually busy.

recommendation.supporting_colours: Use neutral or muted colours to balance strong colours.

examples.assessment: Generally easy to balance because black and white are neutral.
High visual intensity and may look visually busy.

rules.styling_tip: When one item is highly colourful or patterned, keep the remaining major pieces simpler.

rules.name: Pattern colour balance
rules.guideline: When one clothing piece has a strong print or pattern, the remaining pieces should usually use colours taken from the pattern or neutral colours.
recommendations: Match one colour from the print with another outfit piece.
Use neutral bottoms with visually strong printed tops.
Avoid adding multiple competing bold prints unless a deliberate statement look is intended.

examples.outfit: floral shirt + beige trousers + white sneakers
examples.assessment: Balanced because the neutral trousers allow the printed shirt to remain the visual focus.

examples.outfit: printed shirt + solid trousers in a colour from the print
examples.assessment: Cohesive because the trousers repeat an existing colour.

examples.outfit: bold patterned shirt + bold patterned trousers
examples.assessment: High visual complexity and requires careful coordination.

rules.styling_tip: If the print is already visually strong, keep footwear and accessories relatively simple.

rules.name: Colour selection by occasion
rules.guideline: Colour combinations should also be evaluated according to the occasion, dress code and desired level of formality.

office.styling_tip: Prefer controlled contrast and muted colours for a polished professional appearance.

college.styling_tip: Casual combinations can have more flexibility while keeping the overall outfit balanced.

date.styling_tip: Use balanced colours and avoid unnecessary visual clutter.

wedding.styling_tip: Consider the wedding setting, time of day and level of formality before choosing colours.

casual.styling_tip: Casual outfits allow more flexibility in colour and contrast.

rules.name: Colour selection based on skin undertone
rules.guideline: Colour recommendations can consider warm, cool or neutral undertones, but clothing colour suitability is not absolute and personal preference, contrast and styling context also matter.
rules.important_note: Do not reject a colour solely because of skin undertone. Contrast, shade intensity, lighting, personal preference and the complete outfit should also be considered.
rules.styling_tip: When suggesting colours near the face, consider undertone and contrast together rather than using a fixed list of 'allowed' colours.

rules.name: Colour placement and visual proportion
rules.guideline: Colour placement can influence where visual attention is drawn, but it should be treated as a styling tool rather than a strict body-type rule.

principles.effect: A brighter or more contrasting top can draw more visual attention toward the upper body.
A brighter or more contrasting bottom can draw more visual attention toward the lower body.
Similar colours can create visual continuity and may make the outfit appear more streamlined.
Creates clear separation between the upper and lower body.

rules.styling_tip: Use colour placement according to the wearer's preferred visual balance, not as a fixed rule based on body type.

rules.name: Colour interaction with fabric and texture
rules.guideline: The visual effect of a colour can change depending on fabric, texture, finish and lighting.

examples.matte_fabric: Often creates a clean and understated appearance.
examples.shiny_fabric: Can appear more dramatic and attention-grabbing.

examples.textured_fabric: Can create a relaxed and earthy appearance.
examples.smooth_fabric: Can appear cleaner and more refined.

examples.cotton: Usually creates a casual and clean appearance.
examples.linen: Often creates a relaxed and breathable visual impression.

rules.styling_tip: When an outfit contains several textures, keep the colour palette relatively controlled so the outfit does not become visually overwhelming.

rules.name: Colour selection by time of day
rules.guideline: The perceived appearance of colours can change with natural and artificial lighting, so time of day and lighting should be considered when recommending an outfit.

daytime.styling_tip: Lighter and softer colours can work well in bright daytime settings, depending on the occasion.

evening.styling_tip: Deeper colours can create a refined evening appearance, especially when paired with appropriate textures and footwear.

rules.important_note: This is not a strict rule. Venue lighting, dress code, season and personal preference can change the recommendation.

rules.name: Colour selection by season
rules.guideline: Season can influence colour preference, but there are no strict colours that must be worn in a particular season.

summer.styling_tip: Lighter colours can create a fresh and relaxed summer appearance.

monsoon.styling_tip: Darker and practical colours can be easier to manage in wet conditions.

winter.styling_tip: Deeper colours and warm neutrals can work well with winter layers and heavier textures.

rules.important_note: Season should be considered together with weather, occasion, fabric, lighting and personal preference.

rules.name: Footwear colour coordination
rules.guideline: Footwear should support the overall colour palette rather than compete with the main outfit.
rules.styling_tip: Neutral footwear colours are generally versatile. Strongly coloured footwear can be treated as an accent and should be considered with the rest of the outfit.

rules.name: Accessory colour coordination
rules.guideline: Accessories should complement the outfit's colour palette and style without creating unnecessary visual competition.
rules.styling_tip: If the outfit already contains a strong colour or pattern, keep accessories relatively simple. Metallic accessories can work as subtle accents.

rules.name: Layering colour coordination
rules.guideline: When multiple layers are worn, the colours should create a deliberate visual hierarchy rather than making every layer equally dominant.

principles.description: A neutral inner layer can make a stronger outer layer easier to style.
Different shades from the same colour family can create a cohesive layered outfit.
A contrasting outer layer can become the visual focus while simpler colours support it.

examples.outfit: white T-shirt + blue overshirt + beige trousers
examples.assessment: Balanced because the neutral T-shirt and trousers support the blue outer layer.

examples.outfit: black T-shirt + black overshirt + grey trousers
examples.assessment: Creates a controlled dark upper-body palette with a lighter lower-body contrast.

examples.outfit: cream T-shirt + beige overshirt + brown trousers
examples.assessment: Uses warm neutral shades to create a cohesive layered look.

rules.styling_tip: If the outer layer has a bold colour or pattern, keep the inner layer and other major pieces relatively simple.

rules.name: Accent colour usage
rules.guideline: Use one noticeable accent colour with a neutral or muted base to add visual interest without making the outfit look overly busy.
rules.styling_tip: When one item is the main accent, keep the remaining pieces relatively simple and coordinated.

rules.name: Repeat a colour across the outfit
rules.guideline: Repeating one colour in two or more elements can create visual cohesion and make the outfit feel more intentional.
rules.styling_tip: Colour repetition does not need to be exact; similar shades can create coordination while keeping the outfit natural.

rules.name: Limit the main colour palette
rules.guideline: Using around two to three main colours can make an outfit easier to coordinate and visually balanced.
rules.styling_tip: Treat this as a practical guideline rather than a strict rule; patterns, textures and accessories can introduce additional shades.

rules.name: Choose a dominant colour
rules.guideline: A clear dominant colour gives the outfit visual direction, while secondary and accent colours should support it.
good_examples: dominant black + beige trousers + white sneakers
dominant beige + black top + brown accessories
dominant navy + white shirt + brown shoes
dominant olive + cream top + brown accessories
rules.styling_tip: If multiple pieces have equally strong colours, simplify the accessories or footwear to reduce visual competition.

rules.name: Denim colour coordination
rules.guideline: Denim is versatile and can be paired with neutrals, earthy tones and selected colours depending on the denim wash.
rules.styling_tip: Use the denim wash as part of the overall colour balance and consider the top, footwear and accessories together rather than matching only two pieces.

rules.name: Pastel colour coordination
rules.guideline: Pastel colours create a softer visual effect and usually work well with neutrals or other muted shades.
rules.styling_tip: When using a pastel piece, keep the rest of the outfit neutral or muted if you want a clean and easy-to-style appearance.

rules.name: Colour blocking
rules.guideline: Colour blocking uses clearly different colour areas to create a deliberate visual contrast between outfit pieces.
rules.styling_tip: When using strong colour blocking, keep footwear and accessories relatively simple so the main colour contrast remains the focus.

rules.name: Formal and professional colour selection
rules.guideline: Formal outfits generally work well with restrained, neutral and deeper colours that create a polished appearance.
rules.styling_tip: For formal settings, keep highly saturated colours and multiple strong accents limited unless the dress code or occasion calls for them.

rules.name: Festive colour selection
rules.guideline: Festive outfits can use richer, warmer or more noticeable colours while maintaining coordination between the main outfit pieces.
rules.styling_tip: For festive styling, richer colours can be paired with softer neutrals to create visual balance without making the outfit overly busy.

rules.name: Colour coordination with black bottoms
rules.guideline: Black trousers or jeans provide a neutral base and can support a wide range of top colours.
rules.styling_tip: Because black bottoms are visually neutral, choose the top based on the desired contrast, occasion and overall style.

rules.name: Colour coordination with beige bottoms
rules.guideline: Beige trousers provide a warm neutral base and work well with both darker and lighter top colours.
rules.styling_tip: Use darker tops for stronger contrast and lighter or earthy tops for a softer tonal appearance.

rules.name: Colour coordination with grey bottoms
rules.guideline: Grey trousers or jeans provide a neutral foundation and can be paired with both light and dark tops.
rules.styling_tip: Use contrast between the top and grey bottom when you want clearer separation, or similar muted tones for a softer minimal look.

rules.name: Colour coordination with white bottoms
rules.guideline: White trousers or jeans create a bright neutral base and pair well with both muted and deeper colours.
rules.styling_tip: Since white bottoms are visually bright, darker or richer tops can create stronger contrast while muted colours create a softer look.

rules.name: Colour coordination with olive bottoms
rules.guideline: Olive trousers provide an earthy muted base and work well with neutrals, warm tones and selected cool colours.
rules.styling_tip: Keep the top colour controlled when the olive bottom is already paired with other earthy or textured pieces.
